Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:10:1.english: And they are necessary - To teach all of them in the Mishna.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:10:2.english: Because it generates a profit for them - This is our reading.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:11:1.hebrew: דחשיבא ליה מילתא - דצריך ישראל לשאול את כליו, וידע דהדר ליה את כליו בעין:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:11:1.english: Because the matter is significant to him - For a Jew needs to borrow his utensils, and he knows that his utensils will return to him intact.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:14:1.english: She shall not apply lime - She shall not put lime on her face during the intermediate days of the Festival.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:14:2.hebrew: מפני שניוול הוא לה - בעודו על פניה, ואף על פי כשנוטלתו מאדימה ומצהיל פניה, כיון דהנאה זו אינה אלא עד לאחר המועד, וניוול בתוך המועד אסור:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:14:2.english: Because it is a disfigurement for her - While it is on her face. And even though when she removes it, it reddens and brightens her face, [it is forbidden] since this benefit is not until after the Festival, and disfigurement during the Festival is forbidden.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:14:3.english: To fold it back - To remove it from her face.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:14:4.hebrew: בתוך המועד - כגון שבאה לסוד בתחלת המועד, ולבסוף יום או יומים תטלנו, ונהנית הימנו בתוך המועד:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:14:4.english: During the Festival - For example, where she comes to apply lime at the beginning of the Festival, and after a day or two she will remove it, and she derives benefit from it during the Festival.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:15:1.hebrew: דכולהו מיצר עכשיו - כל מה שהתירו לעשות במועד, מיצר הוא באותה שעה, כגון שחיטה ותיקון סעודה, והתירו לו משום שמחה דלאחר זמן שבתוך המועד:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:15:1.english: For all of them, he is distressed now - [With regard to] everything that they permitted to do on the Festival, he is distressed at that time, such as slaughtering and preparing a meal, and they permitted [it] to him because of the joy later on that is within the Festival.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:16:1.hebrew: מלוה בשטר אין נפרעין מהן - לפני אידיהן, מפני ששמח הוא לאחר זמן ביום אידו, דכיון דנקט שטרא ישראל עילויה, כל שעתא מסתפי מיניה:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:16:1.english: [For] a loan with a document, one may not collect payment from them - Before their festivals, because he is happy later on, on the day of his festival; for since the Jew held a document against him, he was afraid of him at all times.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:1:1.english: A person may not extend a cup of wine to a nazirite - Lest he come to drink it.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:1:2.hebrew: ואבר מן החי לבני נח - לפי שנאסר להן, דכתיב אך בשר וגו' (בראשית ט):
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:1:2.english: And a limb from a living [animal] to descendants of Noah - Because it was forbidden to them, as it is written: "However, flesh, etc." (Genesis 9:4).

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:2:1.hebrew: דקיימא בתרי עברי נהרא - עובד כוכבים מצד זה, וישראל מצד זה, דאי לא יהיב ליה, לא מצי שקיל:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:2:1.english: Where they are standing on two sides of a river - An idolater is on this side and an Israelite is on that side, for if he does not give [it] to him, he cannot take [it].

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:3:1.hebrew: נשא ונתן - לפני אידיהן עמהן, מהו בהנאה:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:3:1.english: [If] he engaged in business - Before their festivals with them, what is [the ruling regarding deriving] benefit?

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:3:2.english: It is forbidden - To derive benefit from that merchandise.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:1.english: When they said, "It is forbidden to engage in business with them" - [This refers to] before their festivals.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:2.hebrew: לא אסרו אלא בדבר המתקיים - עד יום אידיהן, דחזי ליה קמיה ביום אידו ואזיל ומודה:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:2.english: They forbade [it] only with regard to an item that endures - Until the day of their festival, for he sees it before him on the day of his festival and goes and gives thanks [to his idol].

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:3.hebrew: אבל דבר שאינו מתקיים - כגון ירק וכיוצא בו, מותר:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:3.english: But an item that does not endure - Such as vegetables and the like, it is permitted.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:4.hebrew: בדבי רבי אושעיא - במתניתא דבי רבי אושעיא, דאיהו סידרה למתניתא, וכן ר' חייא:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:4.english: In the school of Rabbi Oshaya - In the baraita of the school of Rabbi Oshaya, for he arranged the baraita, and likewise Rabbi Chiya.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:5.hebrew: אבל לא לוקחין מהן - דמרווח ליה, שמתוך שאינו מתקיים, מתאוה הוא למכרו:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:5.english: But one may not buy from them - For it brings him relief, as since it does not endure, he is eager to sell it.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:6:1.hebrew: קסרינאה - דינר מצורה חדשה, שפסל קיסר את הראשונה וגזר על זו:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:6:1.english: Caesarean - A dinar of a new design, where the Caesar invalidated the first [one] and decreed [the use of] this [one].

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:6:2.hebrew: כלאחר יד - שלא יבין שמדעת השלכתו, וכיון שרואה שאבד ממך, לא ישמח:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:6:2.english: In an unusual manner - So that he will not realize that you threw it intentionally, and since he sees that it was lost from you, he will not rejoice.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 6b:7:1.english: All of it is because he gives thanks - For the idolater will rejoice when a Jew needs him.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 6b:10:1.hebrew: אלא ללוות מהן מעוטי קא ממעט להו - מכאן ראיה לפר"ת, דמיירי בלא רבית; דמאי קאמר מעוטי קא ממעט להו, אם מלוה ברבית כדי להרויח:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 6b:10:1.english: Rather, to borrow from them, it diminishes [their property] for them - From here is a proof for the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam that [the mishna] is dealing with [a loan] without interest; for why would [the Gemara] say, "it diminishes [their property] for them," if [the gentile] lends with interest in order to make a profit?

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 6b:1:1.hebrew: מנין שלא יושיט אדם כוס יין לנזיר - נראה דה"ה בכל שאר איסורין, אלא להכי נקט כוס יין לנזיר משום דמסתמא למישתי קא בעי ליה, כיון דכ"ע חמרא שתו, ושמא שכח נזירתו. אבל ישראל שאמר הושיט לי נבלה או חזיר או שום איסור, אין לחושדו מלהושיט לו. אבל אם ידוע לו שרוצה לאכלו, אסור להושיט לו, ואפי' הוא שלו, מדקאמר: אי לא יהיב ליה שקיל ליה איהו. ולפי זה, אסור להושיט למומרים לעבודת כוכבים דבר איסור, אע"פ שהוא שלהם, כי הדבר ידוע שיאכלוהו, והוא נאסר להם, דכישראל גמור חשבינן ליה. ומיירי בדקאי במקום שלא יוכל ליקח אם לא יושיט לו זה, וכדמסיק דקאי בתרי עברי נהרא:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 6b:1:1.english: From where [is it derived] that a person may not extend a cup of wine to a nazirite - It appears that the same applies to all other prohibitions; rather, the reason [the Baraita] specified a cup of wine to a nazirite is because he presumably wants it for drinking, since everyone drinks wine, and perhaps he forgot his nazirite vow. However, [in the case of an ordinary] Israelite who says, "Extend to me neveilah [an unslaughtered carcass]," or "pig," or any prohibited item, one need not suspect him [and refrain] from extending it to him. However, if it is known to him that he wants to eat it, it is forbidden to extend it to him, and even [if the item] is his [own], since [the Gemara] says: "If [one] does not give it to him, he would take it himself." And according to this, it is forbidden to extend a prohibited item to apostates to idol worship, even though it is theirs, because it is known that they will eat it, and it is prohibited to them, as we consider [an apostate] a full Israelite [who remains bound by the Torah]. And [this] is dealing with [a case where] he is standing in a place where he cannot take [it] if this [person] does not extend it to him, and as [the Gemara] concludes, where [they are] standing on two opposite banks of a river.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:1.hebrew: תניא כוותיה דרשב"ל - נראה לר"י דהלכה כרבי יוחנן, אע"ג דתניא כוותיה דרשב"ל. ומייתי ראיה מההיא דהחולץ (יבמות לו.), דקא חשיב הני דהלכה כרשב"ל לגבי ר' יוחנן, ולא חשיב הא. ואין לומר, דהא דלא חשיב הא דהכא היינו משום דתניא כוותיה ולא איצטריך למחשבה; דהא חשיב התם חליצת מעוברת, אע"ג דתניא התם נמי כוותיה. ועוד, דלקמן (עבודה זרה דף ז:) מסיק נשא ונתן איכא בינייהו, וקא מפרש דחכמים דמתני' אית להו נשא ונתן אסור כר' יוחנן; ומתניתין עדיפא מברייתא:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:1.english: It is taught in accordance with Reish Lakish - It appears to the Ri that the halakhah is in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan, even though it is taught [in a Baraita] in accordance with Reish Lakish. And he brings proof from that [passage in chapter] HaCholetz (Yevamot 36a), which lists those [cases where] the halakhah is in accordance with Reish Lakish against Rabbi Yochanan, and it does not list this [case]. And one cannot say that the reason it does not list this [case] here is because [a Baraita] is taught in accordance with him, and [therefore] it was not necessary to list it — for behold, it lists there [the case of] the chalitzah of a pregnant woman, even though there too it is taught [in a Baraita] in accordance with him. And furthermore, below (Avodah Zarah 7b), [the Gemara] concludes: "[Whether after the fact] one engaged in business is [the difference] between them," and explains that the Sages of the Mishnah hold that [if] one engaged in business it is prohibited, in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan; and a Mishnah takes precedence over a Baraita.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:2.hebrew: לא אסרו אלא בדבר המתקיים - פירוש: מכר דוקא, דאילו לקנות ודאי אסור בדבר שאינו מתקיים יותר מדבר המתקיים. אלא ודאי לא איירי הך ברייתא אלא במכר, ואפ"ה קרי ליה בסיפא נשא ונתן, כפר"ת; ולפי' הקונטרס קשה:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:2.english: They prohibited only in the case of an item that endures - [This] means specifically selling, for regarding buying, it is certainly forbidden in the case of an item that does not endure even more than an item that endures. Rather, certainly this baraita is dealing only with selling; and even so, in the latter clause [the baraita] calls it "engaged in business" [lit., took and gave], in accordance with the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam; and according to the explanation of Rashi [the Kuntres], it is difficult.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:3.hebrew: אבל לא לוקחין מהם - לפר"ת, דלא אסור שום קניה, צ"ל: לוקחין — קבלת דורון. וה"ה נמי בדבר המתקיים, שאין מקבלין הימנו דורון. ואין לדקדק: הא דבר המתקיים לוקחין, דהא דינר קיסריינא דבר המתקיים הוא:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 6b:5:3.english: But one may not buy from them - According to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam, that no purchase is forbidden at all, one must say [that] "taking" [lokechin, means] receiving a gift. And the same applies also to an enduring item, that one may not receive a gift from him. And one should not infer: "Behold, [in the case of] an enduring item, one may take [a gift]," for a Caesarean dinar is an enduring item [and yet accepting it as a gift was forbidden].

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 6b:9:1.hebrew: אמר אביי גזרה לפרוע מהן אטו לפורען - תימה: למה ליה לאביי למימר משום גזרה? לימא טעמא משום דשמח הוא, כדאמר במתני' אע"פ שהוא מיצר עכשיו שמח הוא לאחר זמן. וי"ל, דמשום האי טעמא דשמח לאחר זמן ליכא (למיגזר), כיון שאינו שמח ביום אידו. ומיהו, אי לאו דאיכא שום שמחה, לא הוה שייך נמי למיגזר; דהא דגזרינן בכולהו, היינו משום דאיכא שום שמחה, כדפריש בסמוך בצריכותא. והשתא ניחא, דאצטריכו כולהו לאביי נמי כמו לרבא:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 6b:9:1.english: Abaye said: [It is] a decree [prohibiting] collecting debts from them lest [one come] to repay them - It is surprising: Why did Abaye need to say [that it is prohibited] because of a decree? Let him say the reason is that he rejoices, as [the Tanna] said in the Mishna: "Even though he is distressed now, he rejoices later"! And one can say that on account of this reason, that he rejoices later, there is no [basis] (to decree) [a prohibition], since he does not rejoice on the day of his festival. However, were it not that there is some joy, it would also not be appropriate to decree [it]; for the fact that we decree in all of them is because there is some joy [involved], as [the Gemara] explains nearby in the [passage establishing the] necessity [of each case]. And now it is well that all of them were necessary according to Abaye as well, just as [they were necessary] according to Rava.
